taylor: Quick report: found a reproducible hang when using the Python SDK stream against servers that half-close (send final chunk then FIN). Our async generator can block forever.

neil: which HTTP client? httpx or aiohttp?

taylor: httpx async. Repro gist: client.stream -> resp.aiter_bytes() sometimes never yields StopAsyncIteration after server closes.

priya: sounds like we treat "no data yet" the same as "connection closed". Can you paste minimal snippet?

taylor: snippet:
```py
async with client.stream("GET", url) as resp:
    async for part in resp.aiter_bytes():
        process(part)
```
server: sends last chunk then closes -> generator blocks on aiter_bytes()

neil: fix idea: add a Stream wrapper that checks transport EOF and converts to StopAsyncIteration. Also provide `aclose()` and context manager semantics so consumers can deterministically close.

priya: +1. Also add a sync wrapper for non-async users: run a background loop with bounded queue and put an EOF sentinel. Document memory/backpressure tradeoffs.

taylor: other wrinkle: auth refresh during active stream replaces connection; current behavior leaves old connection silent and consumers hang. Proposal: emit a StreamState.REPLACED sentinel chunk or raise StreamReplaced error. Typed StreamingChunk should include state: OPEN/CLOSED/REPLACED/ERRORED.

neil: implement StreamingChunk dataclass and export type aliases: Stream (AsyncIterator[StreamingChunk]) and SyncStream (Iterator[StreamingChunk]). Update SDK typing from AsyncIterator[str] to AsyncIterator[StreamingChunk].

priya: tests: write a half-close unit test that simulates server FIN and assert generator ends. Also test cancellation: cancelling consumer must cancel underlying read task and close transport. Avoid weakref.finalize due to event loop shutdown edge cases; prefer explicit aclose().

taylor: added examples/streaming_shutdown.py showing SIGINT handler that calls `await s.aclose()` and a small sync example using `iter_stream()` with `max_queue_size=100`.

neil: small API nicety: add optional `on_close` callback on stream creation so apps can hook metrics without awaiting aclose. Also expose `cancel()` that schedules aclose in the loop for sync callers.

ci-bot: CI run for branch fix/stream-halfclose started. unit test stream_halfclose_test.py failed locally but passes in CI sandbox. See https://ci.redwood/jobs/542

priya: PR opened with Stream type, EOF handling, sync wrapper example, and tests. Ping @neil for review.

neil: reviewed, minor comments on docs and typing. LGTM after fixes.

ci-bot: PR fix/stream-halfclose merged  CI green  https://ci.redwood/pr/4321

taylor: verified on staging against service that half-closes. No more hung generators. Updated migration docs: prefer `async with client.stream(...) as s:` and always `await s.aclose()` if not using context manager. Closing thread. :white_check_mark:
